messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: runtime-cluster-a - high throttle_event rate (>= 5/min) detected by autoscale-observer. Triggered alert group: autoscale/throttle_count.
maya: taking this — I'm on call. starting triage.
alejandro: hey maya — do you have a quick impact read? are customers 503'ing or seeing latency?
maya: initial look: error rate on frontend-proxy is up ~1.8% for requests routed to runtime-cluster-a, but 99th percentile latency is only up ~200ms. There's a spike in token throttles from the serving runtime. No direct 503s seen in customer-facing metrics yet, but a couple of retries visible.
zara: seeing an increase in queued_requests on the same nodes, queue_depth is spiking to 220 for short bursts. autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough.
maya: paging history: throttles start 02:14 UTC, peaked 02:17-02:20. Root cause likely sudden burst from a scheduled batch job hitting a hot model variant.
tom: heads up — that batch job was supposed to be limited to low-priority tier. I'll check scheduler logs.
ops-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-032 - High throttle events @runtime-cluster-a. Severity: P2. Runbook: /runbooks/autoscale-throttle (link)
sre-runbook-bot: maya, steps recommended: 1) put temporary mute on noisy queue-depth alert -> `alert:autoscale/queue_depth` 2) scale up pool or increase burst capacity 3) add short-term routing to fallback model variant.
maya: following runbook: muting queue_depth alert for 30m to reduce noise while we mitigate.
maya: command I ran:
```
# increase dedicated pool by 2 nodes (prod)
redwoodctl cluster scale --cluster runtime-cluster-a --add-nodes 2 --reason "throttle spike triage"
```
alejandro: thanks. I'm seeing the scale request queued, should become active in ~90s. Meanwhile if we divert some traffic to runtime-cluster-b we can relieve the hot nodes.
zara: quick metric checks I ran: `tokens/sec` for the hot variant jumped from avg 180k -> 620k during the spike. Queue depth 99p to 220. throttle_count rate 6.4/min.
maya: mitigation plan: 1) complete scale-up 2) reroute a small % (10-15%) of requests to runtime-cluster-b as fallback 3) add a short-lived override to autoscaler to favor aggressive scaling for 10m 4) create post-incident follow-ups for alert tuning and scheduler policy.
tom: I found the batch job — misconfigured cron, started a parallel run. Rolling kill for the extra job now.
ops-bot: scale-up event applied: +2 nodes on runtime-cluster-a. New capacity reporting in metrics in ~2m.
maya: scale seems active, nodes passing healthchecks. I'm gradually shifting 15% traffic to cluster-b using routing policy `route: degrade-on-saturation` w/ `weight=0.15`.
alejandro: seeing immediate queue_depth drop to ~90 on the previously hot nodes. throttle_count down to 1.1/min. Good.
zara: customer impact: no alerts from customer-facing SLA dashboards. Some increased retries but within retry budget for most clients. Recommend marking customer impact as "low transient".
maya: agreed. I'll update INC-2026-032 to Low Impact.
--- post-mortem / after-action discussion ---
maya: ok that stabilizes things. Now we need to tune alerts and dashboards so we don't get paged for the same noisy pattern. Suggestions?
alejandro: current queue_depth alert fires at 120 (5m avg). In practice short bursts above 200 are transient and self-heal with scaling. We should change logic to: alert when 5m avg > 120 AND sustained 90th-percentile tokens/sec > 300k for same period. That ties queue depth to actual throughput.
zara: +1. Also add a suppression window when autoscaler is actively scaling nodes (so we don't get duplicate pages while it's converging).
tom: propose new tokens/sec threshold for throttle alert: currently the throttle_count alert is absolute (>=5/min). Rather than hard count, we can make it rate-per-100k-tokens: throttle_rate_norm = throttle_count / (tokens/sec/100k). Then alert if throttle_rate_norm > 0.5 for 3m. This avoids paging during very high-volume situations where absolute throttle count grows but rate stays low relative to tokens.
maya: love the normalized approach. It requires a little more metric math in Datadog/Grafana. Let's add it to the dashboard and make it an experimental tuning for 2 weeks.
alejandro: dashboard additions: 1) combined panel: tokens/sec (per model variant) + throttle_rate_norm + queue_depth 2) autoscaler activity overlay (scale events) 3) routing weight changes timeline. I'll make a draft Grafana dashboard and link it.
zara: also create a small alert dedupe rule: if throttles and queue_depth fire within 2m of a scaling event, route both to a low-noise channel `#eng-sre-incidents` instead of paging channel.
maya: action list:
- alejandro: create dashboard PR + export link (owner)
- tom: fix scheduler job config and add validation for parallel runs (owner)
- zara: PR to change alert definition for queue_depth (owner)
- maya: update INC-2026-032 with summary and add follow-up ticket to postmortem repo
- ops-bot: runbook change request to include normalization guidance (owner: ops)

alejandro: putting draft dashboard here: https://grafana.example.com/d/abc123/autoscale-throttle-bakeoff (will add panels and queries).
zara: PR for alert rule created: https://git.example.com/infra/alerting/pulls/42 - set to staging first.
maya: setting follow-up ticket: PMT-789 (post-incident tuning).
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-032 status -> mitigated. Paging suppressed for this incidence.
maya: thanks all. One learning: we need greater visibility on scheduled batch jobs that hit hot model variants — add scheduler -> model-variant tagging so we can pre-emptively route non-interactive jobs.
tom: will add scheduler validation rule. I'll also add a nightly job audit and alert if more than 1 concurrent run detected.
alejandro: +1 to experimental normalization. Let's review results in 2 weeks and then decide whether to promote.
zara: :thumbsup: will monitor and tweak thresholds.
maya: handing off to zara for daytime follow-up. I'm off-call. @zara take lead for the doc and next steps.
zara: taking handoff. I'll create the postmortem draft tomorrow and tag owners.
maya: thanks, good handoff. :white_check_mark:
